title: Closed-item worktree cleanup on WinB has no permitted executor: Codex's exec policy refuses even a checked, non-forced `git worktree remove`
outcome: Worktrees and build outputs of closed items on a satellite (WinB) can be removed through a supported, permitted route after the existing path, ownership and not-in-use checks, without switching tools or executors to get past a policy refusal, so they stop accumulating.
acceptance: The exact refusing layer and rule for the non-forced `git worktree remove` refusal ('CreateProcess ... rejected: blocked by policy') from a Codex root session on WinB are established with evidence: the Codex exec policy under the session's approval policy, the command form or wrapper used, or something TermAl configures. This builds on the completed findings w-c97f4e840563 and w-e2a5af1634f0.

A supported route for closed-item cleanup on a satellite is decided and recorded. Either it is a product route (for example a host-side removal of a released, path-checked worktree) built and tested here, or a configuration route that Greg has explicitly authorized and that is documented. The route keeps the existing checks: path inside the repository, ownership, not in use, item closed.

If a product route is built: behavioural tests cover refusal outside the repository, an in-use worktree, and a successful removal of a released worktree; no text-pinning test; the review pair is clean and the full gate passes.
